retail_vs_institutional_reaction.retail_sentiment_summary: Retail investors on Reddit and FinTwit cheered Nokia's clean headline beat (€5,154M net sales vs €4,980M consensus, comparable operating profit €605M vs €525M), the +123% explosion in AI & Cloud net sales, and the landmark Google €13B Finland partnership. Community discussion centered on deep-value re-rating, noting trailing P/E compressing to ~16.4x forward, supported by the €0.03/sh quarterly dividend (€0.14 annual authorization) and NVIDIA/T-Mobile AI-RAN validation.
retail_vs_institutional_reaction.institutional_sentiment_summary: Institutional desks zeroed in on Network Infrastructure's re-acceleration (+15% CC), driven by IP Networks (+43% CC) and Optical Networks (+18% CC), and the acceleration of Infinera net synergies (€200M one year early). However, portfolio managers were balanced by the working capital drag (-€560M in Q3, leading to -€99M reported FCF) and management's lowered FY26 FCF conversion guide (35%-55%), which explains why after-hours price action remained disciplined at $7.91 (+0.38%).
retail_vs_institutional_reaction.after_hours_movement_driver: Nokia shares traded tightly in after-hours action at $7.91 (+0.38% vs $7.88 close), well inside the ±4.15% options-implied straddle band. The market balanced a strong operational top-line beat (€5.15B vs €4.98B) and optical margin expansion (+220 bps comparable) against the €400M working capital inventory investment and lowered FCF conversion guide.
